analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/developer/test.md (test-run guidance for cluster, prefix-record and media checks) and docs/operations/provider-release.md (a new 'Cluster Runtime Facts' section). No executable code, workflow YAML, scripts or platform code is in the units, so the described behavior is unverified here.

Security-relevant points in provider-release.md, patch hunks around head lines 577-610 and 649-795:
- The release pipeline would add a step after notarization that computes cluster runtime facts and optionally puts a `cluster_runtime` block in the POST /v1/releases payload. The block drives coordinator-derived approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications. It touches A-011, A-017, A-005 and TB-011 in a platform-owned area.
- The docs say the step reads no secret, strips the secret-derived env values (`r2_public_url`, `coordinator_url`), deletes the signing keychain and fails unless the identity is gone, and runs the app CLI under `env -i`. The doc also gates sending on a per-environment variable (`*_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED`), validates the block in `validate`/`prepare`/`stage`/`publish`, and enforces the 64 KiB body limit. These are described as controls but are not visible in source here; the workflow and script implementation (`scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh`, `provider-cluster-runtime-models.py`, `provider-release-publication.py`) need review in the code PR.
- Trust question: the facts are derived from the build's own worker (`--describe-runtime`) plus catalog and CDN metadata, and the coordinator turns them into serving grants and public-traffic qualifications automatically. The docs state qualification is derived from the build's own declaration and records, so authorization of the cluster pairing depends on the integrity of the signed build and of the catalog and CDN data. Whether the coordinator ties this to T-054 and A-017 controls (independent qualification versus self-declared facts) is a platform contract outside the supplied evidence. A human reviewer should confirm that a release-declared block cannot grant public routing without the platform's independent qualification.
- The docs cite a pinned platform commit (df61dd6f...) as evidence; this was not verified.

No concrete regression is evidenced in the supplied text, so findings are empty. needs_deeper_review is true because the real controls are in unseen workflow and script code.
